name: Frontal-orbital advancement (frontal bossing / brow)

lead: Frontal-orbital advancement, also called frontal bossing, is the goal of moving the brow ridge and upper orbital area forward. The payoff people want is a more prominent, masculine upper face and eyes that look more deep-set under a strong brow.

The nearest documented surgery is facial feminization, which usually reduces the brow ridge by grinding or reshaping bone over the frontal sinus, and brow lifts, which change eyebrow position rather than bone projection. Looksmaxxing forum discussion centres on brow lifts and combined surgery trips; no study of cosmetic advancement in people without a craniofacial condition was found.

paras: People pursue this through consultations with craniofacial or facial plastic surgeons, often as part of a larger multi-procedure plan. Brow lifts reposition soft tissue, while bone work reshapes the forehead. Healing takes weeks to months before the final shape is visible.

Cranioplasty-type bone surgery carries risks of improper bone healing, bone fragment movement and cyst formation, and thin sinus walls complicate bone work near the forehead. Outcome data for forehead and orbit procedures are limited. It is major surgery under general anaesthesia, so surgeon experience and a realistic consultation matter.

angle.text: The aim is a more projected brow and forehead, which gives a stronger, more masculine upper face and deeper-set eyes. It works by moving the brow ridge and upper orbit forward, or by repositioning brow tissue. Published surgery covers brow lifts and brow reduction rather than cosmetic advancement.

lead: In looksmaxxing usage, frontal-orbital advancement and frontal bossing refer to surgery or other changes meant to push the brow ridge and upper orbital area forward, producing a more prominent forehead and brow. The sources reviewed contain little direct material on this exact aim.

The nearest documented surgical literature is facial feminization surgery, which usually reduces rather than advances the brow ridge and forehead [1][2], and brow-lift procedures that change eyebrow position rather than bone projection [3][4]. No study of cosmetic frontal-orbital advancement in a non-craniofacial-condition population was found.
infobox: More forward brow and forehead projection
Brow lift, forehead contouring, orbital rim work

paras: Wikipedia's facial feminization surgery article describes the male brow ridge as typically more horizontal and solid, and procedures that grind it down, or reshape the bone above the frontal sinus when the sinus wall is thin [1]. It states that data on which forehead approach is better is limited, and that female orbits tend to be smaller and higher [1].

A review of facial feminization surgery describes it as a group of procedures changing a male face toward a female one, mainly for transgender women [2]. These procedures move in the opposite direction to the forward brow some looksmaxxers describe.

No studies found on cosmetic forward advancement of the brow and orbit for appearance. Related published work concerns brow lifts, including botulinum toxin brow elevation [3], endoscopic brow lift in 538 patients [4], and the direct brow lift [5].

Looksmax.org members post about brow lifts, often as part of combined surgery packages abroad with other procedures such as genioplasty, cheek implants and canthopexy. These threads concern brow-lift surgery and recovery, not bone advancement.
